title: Multiplying a Four-Digit Number By a One-Digit Number: Finding Missing Digits

sections.normalized_html:
From left to right, what are the missing digits in the following multiplication problem?

[MATH: 1|8|5|2; ×|7; 1|[math]\phantom{i}[/math]|9|[math]\phantom{i}[/math]|4]
sections.readable_text:
From left to right, what are the missing digits in the following multiplication problem?

[MATH: 1|8|5|2; ×|7; 1|[math]\phantom{i}[/math]|9|[math]\phantom{i}[/math]|4]

sections.normalized_html:
First, we multiply the ones:

[MATH: _(1); 1|8|5|2; ×|7; 4|2 × 7 = 14; Carry:1; Write:4]

Next, we multiply the tens:

[MATH: _(3)|_(1); 1|8|5|2; ×|7; 6|4|5 × 7 = 35and1 + 35 = 36; Carry:3; Write:6]

Next, we multiply the hundreds:

[MATH: _(5)|_(3)|_(1); 1|8|5|2; ×|7; 9|6|4|8 × 7 = 56and3 + 56 = 59; Carry:5; Write:9]

Finally, we multiply the thousands:

[MATH: _(5)|_(3)|_(1); 1|8|5|2; ×|7; 1|[math]\color{red}2[/math]|9|6|4|1 × 7 = 7and5 + 7 = 12; Carry:−; Write:12]

Therefore, the missing digits, from left-to-right, are [MATH: \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}2}] and [MATH: \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}6}.]
